newsitem.title: MEXICO: Moderna sees cigarette exports higher.
newsitem.headline: Moderna sees cigarette exports higher.

text.p: Mexican conglomerate Empresas La Moderna SA said it expects its cigarette exports to boom this year and next and sees a gradual recovery in its Mexican marketplace.

The company expects exports to grow 80 percent this year and an additional 30 percent next year largely due to the introduction of its medium-priced Montana brand to Asia, CEO Alfonso Romo told Reuters.
La Moderna's cigarette exports have grown steadily in recent years, from about $17 million in 1994 to $27 million last year.
Romo also said Mexico's cigarette market should begin to recover from the effects of the 1994 peso devaluation.
Although cigarette sales are relatively inelastic here, many Mexican consumers downgraded to cheaper brands that had lower margins for the company.
"We can't say a recovery has begun, but the downshifting has stopped, which is very positive. All we can do from here is gain margin," he said in an interview.

The company's cigarette division accounted for about half of the more than 10 billion pesos in 1995 revenues for La Moderna, which in recent years has diversified into agrobiotechnology, fresh produce and packaging.

Although the company is diversifying away from its core cigarette business, Romo said he did not expect his tobacco unit to be hurt by the health concerns and litigation that have plagued U.S. tobacco companies in recent years.
"What happens in the United States will not necessarily happen in the rest of the world," he said.
